rows.name: One-command skill install
rows.offer: One npx command downloads a skill or a whole skills repository and wires it into the user's coding agent.

flisk.reason: Flisk skills install with this command via flisk-sh/flisk-skills and `flisk project` writes its bundled skills, but Flisk has no installer for arbitrary third-party skills.

rows.name: Install to many coding agents
rows.offer: The CLI detects installed agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and dozens more) and writes the skill into each one's own skills folder.

flisk.reason: Flisk writes both .claude/skills (Claude Code) and .agents/skills (Codex, Cursor and others) but does not target each of the other agents' own folders.

rows.name: Symlink or copy install mode
rows.offer: Skills are installed as symlinks to one canonical copy by default, or as independent copies with a flag.

flisk.reason: The Flisk repo links .agents/skills to .claude/skills with symlinks, but the files `flisk project` writes into a new project are plain copies with no mode choice.

rows.name: Project or global skill scope
rows.offer: Skills install into the current project by default, or into the user's home with -g so every project sees them.

flisk.reason: Flisk skills describe one project's stack and are written into that project; a global skills location is the installer's concern, not the runtime's.

rows.name: Check and update installed skills
rows.offer: `skills check` reports which installed skills have newer upstream versions and `skills update` pulls only the changed ones.

flisk.reason: Skills `flisk project` copies into a project go stale after `flisk upgrade`, and agents then follow old command syntax, so a refresh step fits Flisk.

rows.acceptance: `flisk upgrade` (cli/src/commands/upgrade.ts) or a `flisk project` refresh flag rewrites the project's agent skills from cli/templates/agent-skills; proved by a text check for agent-skills in upgrade.ts and a CLI test.

ice.basis: Impact: stale skills make agents emit wrong flisk commands in every project created before an upgrade. Confidence: skills.sh docs describe update clearly, and upgrade.ts has no skills handling today. Ease: installAgentSkills in cli/src/utils/agent-skills.ts already writes the files, but upgrade needs project detection and overwrite rules.

rows.name: Skills shipped inside npm packages
rows.offer: An experimental sync command links skills that a dependency ships (a root SKILL.md or skills/<name>/SKILL.md) into the project and keeps them tied to the installed version.

flisk.reason: The @flisk-sh/flisk package ships its skills only under templates/agent-skills, not at skills/<name>/SKILL.md, so npm-based skill sync cannot find them; shipping them there would keep skills versioned with the CLI.

rows.acceptance: cli/package.json `files` includes a skills/ folder with each Flisk SKILL.md and scripts/check-npm-package.mjs asserts it; proved by file and text evidence.

ice.basis: Impact: only users who adopt the experimental npm sync benefit, and Flisk already has flisk project and flisk-skills. Confidence: the feature is flagged experimental in the CLI docs. Ease: the skills already exist in cli/templates/agent-skills, so it is a files entry plus a package check in scripts/check-npm-package.mjs.

rows.name: SKILL.md name and description format
rows.offer: A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md whose frontmatter requires a name and a description, so any agent can load it.

rows.name: Standard skill folder discovery
rows.offer: The CLI finds skills in skills/, .claude/skills, .agents/skills and many agent-specific folders in a repository.

rows.name: Claude plugin manifest discovery
rows.offer: Skills declared in .claude-plugin/marketplace.json or plugin.json are discovered too, for compatibility with Claude Code plugin marketplaces.

rows.name: Hide work-in-progress skills
rows.offer: A metadata.internal flag in the frontmatter keeps a skill out of normal discovery unless an env var is set.

flisk.reason: Flisk keeps repo-only skills out of the shared set with a LOCAL list that the sync script honours, not with a per-skill frontmatter flag.

rows.name: Whole skill set in one install
rows.offer: A repository or pack of many skills installs in one command, and users can pick individual skills with --skill.

flisk.reason: flisk-sh/flisk-skills installs as one set and `flisk project` writes the full Flisk set, but a single skill cannot be selected through Flisk itself.

rows.name: Hosted pack builder with sign-in
rows.offer: Signed-in teams build unlisted packs that mix public skills, private files and GitHub repositories behind a shareable install URL.

flisk.reason: A hosted account service for sharing skill bundles is a directory product; Flisk is a local runtime and shares skills through a plain Git repository.

rows.name: Search for skills
rows.offer: `skills find` searches the catalog interactively or by keyword, optionally limited to an owner.

flisk.reason: Discovering third-party skills is the directory's job; Flisk only needs its own skills found, and llms.txt already points agents to them.

rows.name: Run a skill without installing
rows.offer: `skills use` prints a prompt for one skill or launches an agent with it, without writing files into the project.

flisk.reason: Flisk skills are plain Markdown an agent can read from the repository, so a separate ephemeral-use mode does not belong in the runtime.

rows.name: Skill authoring template
rows.offer: `skills init` scaffolds a SKILL.md template so authors can start a new skill.

flisk.reason: Authoring generic skills is not a runtime task; Flisk's own skills are written in flisk-sh/flisk-skills.

rows.name: Install from any Git host or archive
rows.offer: Sources can be GitHub shorthand, any Git URL including private repositories, local paths, or zip and tar downloads.

flisk.reason: Fetching skills from arbitrary sources is installer logic; Flisk does not install third-party skills.

rows.name: Install-based leaderboard
rows.offer: Skills are ranked all-time, trending in 24 hours and hot by install counts the CLI reports.

flisk.reason: Ranking public skills by usage needs a hosted service and install telemetry; Flisk is local-only and deliberately collects none.

rows.name: Anonymous telemetry with opt-out
rows.offer: The CLI reports anonymous install data that feeds the leaderboard, and DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 turns it off.

flisk.reason: Flisk goes further than an opt-out: the CLI sends no telemetry at all.

text.contains: Flisk has no telemetry or analytics

rows.name: Per-skill security audit ratings
rows.offer: Each listed skill gets combined audit results from three scanners, shown as safe, low, medium or high risk.

flisk.reason: Auditing a public catalog of third-party skills is the directory's role; Flisk installs only its own skills.

rows.name: Scan own skills for malicious content
rows.offer: The directory runs routine audits on skill contents for malicious material and points reporters to a security contact.

flisk.reason: Flisk's own skills ship inside the npm package that Socket and Snyk already scan, and a scorer checks that every command in a skill exists, but no scanner reads the skill text itself.

rows.name: Public catalog and search API
rows.offer: A JSON API lists the leaderboard, searches skills and returns per-skill details and audit results, authenticated with Vercel OIDC tokens.

flisk.reason: Exposing a skills catalog over an API is a hosted-directory feature, and Flisk's machine interface is its MCP server.

rows.name: Group skills on the repo page
rows.offer: A skills.sh.json file at the repository root groups a repo's skills into titled sections on its skills.sh page.

flisk.reason: flisk-sh/flisk-skills has 20+ skills, and sections such as setup, recipes and operations would make its skills.sh page scannable.

rows.acceptance: A skills.sh.json with groupings is mirrored by scripts/sync-flisk-skills.sh or a test checks that every grouped name exists in .claude/skills; proved by file evidence.

ice.basis: Impact: only changes how one directory page looks. Confidence: the format is fully specified on the customize page. Ease: the file belongs in the separate flisk-skills repo, so this repo only needs a sync or parity check in scripts/sync-flisk-skills.sh.

rows.name: Install count README badge
rows.offer: Repos can embed a skills.sh badge in their README that shows the install count and links to the skill page.

flisk.reason: Flisk already shows several npm and CI badges in its README, and one for its skills would show agent-skill reach.

rows.acceptance: README.md contains a skills.sh/b/flisk-sh/flisk-skills badge; proved by a text evidence on README.md.

ice.basis: Impact: a small social-proof signal only. Confidence: the badge URL pattern is documented. Ease: one line in the README badge block.

rows.name: Official publisher listing
rows.offer: An Official page lists skills published by the makers of each technology, with repository and skill counts.

flisk.reason: Being featured is an editorial decision of the directory, not something Flisk can build.
